summary: The meta skill router is justified by real demand, but on the current real-corpus suite it degraded because the injected router guidance over-routed naming/taxonomy governance prompts into sub_skills/new instead of treating them as outside the current four-route surface.
strengths: Real-corpus create/improve/validate/evaluate requests still route correctly.
Operational false-positive guard worked for Git/GitHub overlap and out-of-scope domain work.
The cluster is not dead weight; it clearly maps to recurrent repo work.
weaknesses: Naming, taxonomy, and governance prompts are common enough to matter but are not represented as a first-class route.
The current router wording is cleaner than the real corpus and can over-trigger on broad meta architecture conversations.
Behavioral benchmark/evaluate language is overrepresented in docs relative to the actual prompt distribution.

primary_failure_case.prompt: skillの命名規則も決めていかないとと思っています。skill- で良いか、dotnet- や python- から入るべきか意見を聞きたいです。
primary_failure_case.why_it_matters: This is a real-corpus governance question, not a direct create/improve/validate/evaluate request. Forcing it into new increases trigger competition and makes the router feel more chaotic than helpful.

recommendations: Revise the router to explicitly mention naming/taxonomy/governance as a non-router or separate route decision.
Add more real-corpus near-miss examples to the parent router so broad meta discussions do not default to sub_skills/new.
Keep evaluate, but do not let benchmark vocabulary dominate the router narrative until real usage grows.
